uic406.publisher: International Union of Railways (UIC), Code 406, Capacity, 2nd edition, June 2013
uic406.about: The method planners use to measure how full a line is: the time each train keeps each block (route formation, approach, run through the block, clearing, release), the trains of an hour pushed together, and the share of the hour they take; proposed limits of 75% in the busiest hour on lines with mixed trains and on high-speed lines, 85% on lines for suburban trains only

mr_etcs.publisher: A. Trümpi (Swiss Federal Railways), ETCS Level 2: success for the Swiss Federal Railways, European Railway Review, 6 June 2007
mr_etcs.about: New line from Mattstetten to Rothrist: ETCS level 2 in full operation since 18 March 2007, 242 passenger trains a day, speeds raised from 160 to 200 km/h at the end of 2007; operational headways of less than two minutes at 200 km/h stated as necessary

tl_ato.publisher: Rail Technical Strategy (Great Britain), case study: Thameslink core, September 2020
tl_ato.about: Thameslink: automatic driving over ETCS level 2 in use on the central route since March 2018, to go from 16 to 24 trains an hour

tsi_hs_brake.publisher: European Commission, Decision 2008/232/EC, technical specification for interoperability of high-speed rolling stock, clause 4.2.4 (braking), tables 6 and 8
tsi_hs_brake.about: Least braking of a high-speed train on level track. Emergency braking, case B (reduced grip, part of the brakes out of use), felt after 3 s: 0.60 m/s² from 350 to 300 km/h, 0.7 from 300 to 230, 0.8 from 230 to 170, 0.9 from 170 to 0. Service braking, felt after 2 s: 0.30, 0.35, 0.6 and 0.6 m/s² over the same speeds

epsf_f018.publisher: Établissement public de sécurité ferroviaire (EPSF), SAM F 018, braking performance of rolling stock on lines fitted with TVM, version 1, 2 July 2009
epsf_f018.about: French rule for trains on high-speed lines: service and emergency braking as in the European specification, requirements set on level track, emergency brake fully applied within 3 seconds

era_curves.publisher: European Union Agency for Railways, Introduction to ETCS braking curves, ERA_ERTMS_040026, version 1.5
era_curves.about: How the European signalling works out the point where a train must start braking; worked examples with 9 s for the driver between the indication and the permitted speed, 4 s between the permitted speed and the automatic braking, 2.5 s for the emergency brake of a high-speed train to act; a factor of 0.893 for wet rails in the high-speed example
